title: Strain Engineering of the Topological Gap and Tunable Chern Numbers in the 2D Kagome Metal-Organic Framework Eu$_2$(C$_6$H$_4$)$_3$
authors: Jiaxuan Guo, Simin Nie, Fritz B. Prinz
abstract: The quantum anomalous Hall effect carries dissipationless chiral edge currents without an external magnetic field, yet raising its operating temperature and controlling the number of edge channels remain difficult. Using first-principles calculations, we identify the two-dimensional metal-organic kagome ferromagnet Eu$_2$(C$_6$H$_4$)$_3$ as an intrinsic Chern insulator whose topological gap can be enlarged by mechanical strain. The monolayer has a spin-orbit-coupling-induced gap of 72.7 meV that widens to 124.7 meV under -8% biaxial strain, realizing a quantum anomalous Hall phase with Chern number $\mathcal{C}=-1$ and a single chiral edge state. The local moments come from the half-filled Eu $4f^{7}$ shell, while the gap-opening spin-orbit coupling is carried by Eu $5d$ states hybridized into the carbon kagome bands. The AB-stacked bilayer couples ferromagnetically and accumulates the per-layer Chern numbers, giving $\mathcal{C}=-2$ with two co-propagating chiral channels. An out-of-plane electric field then drives the bilayer through a sequence of topological transitions among $\mathcal{C}=-2$, $-3$, and $-1$, switching the number of edge channels. Together, strain, stacking, and gating give three distinct handles on the gap and the Chern number within a single stoichiometric material.
summary: This theoretical study investigates the tunable topological properties of the 2D metal-organic framework $	ext{Eu}_2(	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_4)_3$. Using DFT calculations, the authors show that the material functions as a controllable Chern insulator. By applying strain, stacking, and electric fields, they demonstrate three distinct methods to manipulate both the size of the topological gap and the quantized Chern number, offering a versatile platform for quantum electronics.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is improving the operating temperature and controlling the number of edge channels in the Quantum Anomalous Hall Effect (QAHE).
main_result: The study demonstrates that mechanical strain, stacking, and out-of-plane electric fields can independently tune both the topological gap and the Chern number in the single material $	ext{Eu}_2(	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_4)_3$.
method: The research relies heavily on first-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations, supplemented by tight-binding models derived from maximally localized Wannier functions to characterize the topological invariants.
model_or_system: The physical system is the two-dimensional metal-organic kagome ferromagnet $	ext{Eu}_2(	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_4)_3$. The electronic properties are modeled as an intrinsic Chern insulator whose topology is sensitive to external perturbations.
key_observables: Chern number ($\mathcal{C}$), topological gap size, Hall conductance, strain ($\epsilon$), and out-of-plane electric field ($E_{	ext{out-of-plane}}$).
important_parameters: The initial SOC gap is $72.7 	ext{ meV}$, which widens to $124.7 	ext{ meV}$ under $-8\%$ biaxial strain. The system exhibits Chern numbers of $\mathcal{C}=-1$ (monolayer) and $\mathcal{C}=-2$ (bilayer).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the topological gap opening is primarily sourced by the hybridization between C-$p$ states and the $	ext{Eu}$ $5d$ states, and that the material remains stable under applied strain and fields.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the atomic structure, phonon dispersion, and AIMD simulations confirming stability. Band structure plots show the evolution of the topological gap under varying strain, while theoretical calculations map out the transitions between different Chern number phases.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the material's stability and intrinsic topological properties (monolayer, $C=-1$). It then systematically explores the tunability by applying mechanical strain (widening the gap) and stacking (achieving $C=-2$). Finally, it introduces an out-of-plane electric field to drive the system through multiple topological transitions.
why_interesting: This work provides a clear, multi-faceted blueprint for engineering topological electronic states using purely structural and electric field controls, which is highly relevant for designing novel quantum devices.

Figure 1(a) depicts the atomic configuration of the monolayer Eu2(C6H4)3. The monolayer crystallizes in the hexagonal space group P6/m: each Eu atom sits at the center of a triangle of three benzene rings, and the corner-sharing triangles trace out a 2D metal-organic kagome lattice. After full relaxation the in-plane lattice constant is a = 13.84 ˚A. We first evaluated the dynamical stability. The phonon dispersion along the high-symmetry lines, shown in Figs. 1(c) and 1(d), contains no imaginary branch, so the monolayer is dynamically stable. Thermal stability was then probed by ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) on a 2 × 2 × 1 supercell: over 3 ps at 300 K the framework remains intact...
